title: Representable free finite-group quotient of a scheme affine over its base
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $p:X\to S$ an affine morphism [pqf-def-affine-morphism], and $K$ a finite group acting on $X$ by $S$-automorphisms. Write $K_S=\coprod_{k\in K}S$, with multiplication induced by that of $K$, and let $a:K_S\times_SX\to X$ be the action. Assume the action is free, meaning that $j=(a,\operatorname{pr}_2):K_S\times_SX\to X\times_SX$ is a monomorphism: it is injective on morphisms from every test $S$-scheme [def-pc-fibre-product]. There exist an $S$-scheme $Q$ and an invariant morphism $q:X\to Q$ which represents the fppf sheafification [def-pc-fppf-site, def-weil-pbc-sheafification] of the orbit presheaf $T\mapsto X(T)/K_S(T)$ on $S$-schemes, where $K_S(T)$ is the group of locally constant maps $|T|\to K$. The map $q$ is finite locally free [def-pc-finite-locally-free] and surjective, and $j$ induces an isomorphism $K_S\times_SX\simeq X\times_QX$. Moreover for every $S'\to S$ the map $q_{S'}:X\times_SS'\to Q\times_SS'$ represents the analogous fppf orbit sheaf for the base-changed action. In particular it is categorical for invariant morphisms to arbitrary $S'$-schemes: each such morphism factors uniquely through $q_{S'}$. No connectedness or etaleness of $X\to S$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 07S7 (spaces-properties-lemma-quotient-scheme), affine case; finite locally free and kernel-pair conclusions from Tag 03BM (groupoids-proposition-finite-flat-equivalence); categorical and base-change properties are the represented orbit-sheaf interpretation of the fppf torsor conclusion.

proof.text: Representable functors are fppf sheaves. Indeed, for an fppf covering and any affine open $V$ of its target, the images of affine opens in the inverse images of $V$ form an open cover of $V$: the covering maps are open by flat-lfp openness. Quasi-compactness of $V$ selects finitely many such images, so the covering is fpqc by its definition. Apply fpqc descent of morphisms; the descended morphism is over $S$ because that equality holds on the cover. Put $P(T)=X(T)/K_S(T)$ and $F=P^\#$. The unit $P\to F$ becomes an isomorphism on sheafification by the universal property and idempotence. The local-bijection criterion therefore says both that sections of $F$ locally lift to $P$ and that two sections of $P$ with equal images in $F$ become equal on a covering. These assertions may be used on the small universe-bounded site of the statement.

source.place: Tag 023Q (lemma-fpqc-universal-effective-epimorphisms); Topologies Tag 022C; sheafification universal property and local-bijection criterion

proof.text: Choose an affine open cover $(U_i)$ of $S$. Write $X_i=p^{-1}(U_i)=\operatorname{Spec}A_i$, affine by the definition of an affine morphism. The action preserves $X_i$, and $R_i=K_{U_i}\times_{U_i}X_i$ is the finite disjoint union of copies of $X_i$, hence affine. Its projection to $X_i$ is locally, on an affine open $\operatorname{Spec}D$ of $X_i$, the spectrum of the diagonal map $D\to\prod_KD$. The standard coordinate vectors give this algebra a finite $D$-basis, so the finite-free algebra spectrum lemma makes this projection finite locally free there. Finiteness is local on the target, and flatness and local finite presentation are local directly from their local-ring and affine-neighbourhood definitions; thus the projection is finite locally free globally. The automorphism $(k,x)\mapsto(k,kx)$ of $R_i$, with inverse $(k,y)\mapsto(k,k^{-1}y)$, makes the action map another finite locally free projection. On every test scheme the image of $(a,\operatorname{pr}_2)$ is an equivalence relation: identity, inverse and multiplication give reflexivity, symmetry and transitivity. Freeness gives injectivity, so $R_i$ identifies with that relation, rather than merely mapping onto it.

source.place: Tag 07S7 (lemma-quotient-scheme), first paragraph; explicit constant-group specialization

proof.text: Apply the affine finite locally free relation quotient theorem to $X_i,R_i$ over $U_i$. With $s=\operatorname{pr}_2$ and $t=a$, its invariant ring is $C_i=\{b\in A_i:s^\sharp(b)=t^\sharp(b)\}$, equivalently $A_i^K$. It supplies $M_i=\operatorname{Spec}C_i$ over $U_i$, representing the fppf orbit sheaf, a finite locally free surjection $q_i:X_i\to M_i$, and the comparison isomorphism $R_i\simeq X_i\times_{M_i}X_i$ with its two prescribed projections. All its hypotheses were checked in the preceding step. The relation on test points is exactly the action of $K_{U_i}(T)$, including locally constant elements on disconnected $T$.

source.place: Tag 03BM (proposition-finite-flat-equivalence), applied to the action relation

proof.text: For each $i$ let $F_i\subset F$ be the subfunctor that equals $F(T)$ when the structure map $T\to S$ factors through $U_i$, and is empty otherwise. This is a sheaf: factorization through an open can be checked on any surjective covering. On schemes over $U_i$, the presheaf $P$ is precisely $T\mapsto X_i(T)/K_{U_i}(T)$. The unit into the restriction of $F$ is locally bijective by step 1: all covers of such a $T$, and their refinements, are still schemes over $U_i$. Hence the local-bijection criterion and the sheafification universal property identify this restriction with the orbit sheaf represented by $M_i$ in step 3. Extending to $S$-schemes identifies $F_i$ with $h_{M_i}$, since neither has sections when $T\to S$ does not factor through $U_i$. For a section $z\in F(T)$, its pullback of $F_i$ is represented by the open subscheme $T\times_SU_i$: on every $T'$ over $T$, membership of $z|_{T'}$ in $F_i(T')$ means exactly that $T'\to S$ factors through $U_i$. Thus each inclusion is representable by open immersions. These opens cover $T$, so the $F_i$ cover $F$. No affineness of $U_i\cap U_j$ is used.

source.place: Tag 07S7 affine case, restriction to affine base opens; Schemes Tag 01JJ (lemma-glue-functors), verification of its subfunctors

proof.text: The sheaf $F$ is in particular a Zariski sheaf. Step 4 verifies all three open-subfunctor conditions of the scheme representability criterion, so obtain an $S$-scheme $Q$ representing $F$. Yoneda turns the composite $h_X\to P\to F=h_Q$ into $q:X\to Q$ over $S$. It is invariant because its first map identifies orbits. Under the representation in step 4, $Q\times_SU_i=M_i$ and $q$ restricted over $U_i$ is the actual $q_i$, since both are induced by the same orbit map. These identities fix the comparison maps, not just their isomorphism classes.

source.place: Tag 01JJ (lemma-glue-functors), as used in Spaces Properties Tag 07S6

proof.text: The opens $M_i=Q\times_SU_i$ cover $Q$. On their inverse images $q$ is the finite locally free surjection $q_i$. Finiteness follows from the finite-local-on-target theorem; flatness follows on the same local rings, and at every point local finite presentation is witnessed by the affine neighbourhoods for $q_i$. Thus $q$ is finite locally free by definition, and it is surjective since each $q_i$ is. The comparison $K_S\times_SX\to X\times_QX$ restricts on this cover to the comparison isomorphisms of step 3. Their inverses agree on overlaps because they are inverses to the same map. They glue uniquely to a global inverse (glue the morphisms on this Zariski, hence fpqc, open cover). This proves the required kernel-pair isomorphism globally.

source.place: Tags 07S6 and 07S7, finite locally free and relation conclusions; Morphisms Tag 01WI

proof.text: Fix any $S'\to S$ and put $X'=X\times_SS'$, $Q'=Q\times_SS'$. The map $q$ is an fppf covering, since it is flat, locally of finite presentation and surjective. The fppf base-change lemma makes $q':X'\to Q'$ an fppf covering; the finite-morphism base-change lemma also makes it finite. Thus $q'$ is finite locally free and surjective. The fibre-product universal property base changes the already constructed kernel pair to $K_{S'}\times_{S'}X'\simeq X'\times_{Q'}X'$ with the same action and projection. Explicitly both sides parametrize, over a test $S'$-scheme $T$, pairs of lifts to $X$ with equal images in $Q$, with their fixed map to $S'$; the original comparison sends $(k,x)$ to $(kx,x)$.

source.place: Tag 021O (lemma-fppf), part (3); Morphisms finite base change; base change of the kernel pair of Tag 07S7

proof.text: For a test $S'$-scheme $T$, invariant $q'$ gives a map $P'(T)=X'(T)/K_{S'}(T)\to Q'(T)$. If two representatives have the same image, the kernel-pair isomorphism in step 7 gives $k\in K_{S'}(T)$ carrying one to the other, so this map is injective. For any $z:T\to Q'$, the fppf covering $T\times_{Q'}X'\to T$ supplies a lift; hence the map is locally surjective. The local-bijection criterion identifies its sheafification with $h_{Q'}$, already an fppf sheaf by step 1. This proves that the particular base-changed $q'$ represents the orbit sheaf; it does not assert that arbitrary invariants commute with arbitrary scalar extension.

source.place: Tag 03C5 (lemma-criterion-quotient-representable), quotient criterion; Tag 07S7, torsor interpretation

proof.text: Let $Y$ be any $S'$-scheme and $f:X'\to Y$ invariant. For every $T$ it induces $P'(T)\to Y(T)$, sending an orbit to the composite with $f$. This is well defined also for locally constant $k$: on the clopen pieces where $k$ is constant invariance gives equality, and the morphisms agree globally by their sheaf property. Naturality is composition. Since $h_Y$ is an fppf sheaf, the universal property of sheafification extends this natural map uniquely to $h_{Q'}\to h_Y$. Yoneda yields a unique $S'$-morphism $Q'\to Y$ whose composite with $q'$ is $f$. For uniqueness, the same universal property identifies any two such natural transformations. This works for every $S'\to S$ and every $Y$, with no connectedness or etaleness assumption on $X\to S$.
